documents.title: Parental Leave Policy (HP-HR-104)
documents.text:
# Parental Leave Policy (HP-HR-104)

Harbor & Pine supports employees who welcome a child through birth, adoption, or foster placement. This policy applies to all US and Canada employees; regional offices publish local supplements.

## Eligibility

- You must have completed **6 months** of continuous employment on the date the child arrives.
- Part-time employees working 20 hours or more per week are eligible on a pro-rated basis.
- Both parents may take leave if both work at Harbor & Pine.

## Paid weeks

| Caregiver role | Paid weeks | Pay rate |
|---|---|---|
| Primary caregiver | 18 weeks | 100% of base salary |
| Secondary caregiver | 8 weeks | 100% of base salary |

The leave may be taken in up to **two blocks**, and all weeks must be used within **12 months** of the birth or placement. Unused weeks are forfeited and are not paid out on termination.

## How to request

1. Notify your manager and People Operations at least **8 weeks** before the expected start date (or as soon as practical for adoption).
2. Submit the request in Compass under *Time Off > Parental*.
3. People Operations confirms benefits continuation and the return date in writing.

## Returning to work

Employees returning from parental leave can use a **phased return**: four weeks at 60% schedule with full pay. Lactation rooms are available on every office floor; see the facilities guide for locations.

Questions: people-ops@harborpine.example

documents.title: Sick Leave Policy (HP-HR-107)
documents.text:
# Sick Leave Policy (HP-HR-107)

Sick leave is separate from vacation and from parental leave. It covers your own illness or injury, medical appointments, and caring for an ill family member.

## Allowance

- Every full-time employee receives **12 paid sick days** per calendar year, credited on January 1.
- New hires receive a pro-rated allowance in their first year.
- Up to **5 unused sick days** carry over into the next year; anything above that expires on December 31.

## Notification

- Tell your manager before your scheduled start time, or within 2 hours of it for warehouse shift workers.
- Record the absence in Compass under *Time Off > Sick*.

## Medical documentation

A doctor's note is **only required after 3 consecutive sick days**. We do not ask for documentation for shorter absences. Notes go to People Operations, never to your manager, and are stored as Restricted data.

## Extended illness

If an illness lasts longer than your remaining sick days, short-term disability insurance starts after **7 calendar days** of absence and pays 70% of base salary for up to 26 weeks. People Operations will contact you to start the claim.

## What sick leave is not for

Sick leave cannot be used to extend vacation, and it is not a substitute for bereavement leave or parental leave, which have their own policies (HP-HR-109 and HP-HR-104).

documents.title: Bereavement Leave Policy (HP-HR-109)
documents.text:
# Bereavement Leave Policy (HP-HR-109)

We know that losing someone close is hard. This policy gives you time to grieve, attend services, and handle family matters without using vacation.

## Paid days

| Relationship | Paid days |
|---|---|
| Immediate family: spouse or partner, child, parent, sibling | 5 working days |
| Extended family: grandparent, grandchild, aunt, uncle, in-law, cousin | 2 working days |
| Close friend or other household member | 1 working day |

Days do not need to be consecutive, but they must be used within **60 days** of the death.

## Travel allowance

If the funeral or memorial requires travel of more than **500 km** one way, you may take up to **3 additional unpaid days**. Managers may approve using vacation days instead of unpaid days.

## Pregnancy loss

Employees who experience a miscarriage or stillbirth, and their partners, receive 5 paid working days under this policy.

## Requesting bereavement leave

- Let your manager know as soon as you can; a short message is enough.
- Record it in Compass under *Time Off > Bereavement*. No death certificate or proof is required.

## Support

The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offers six free counselling sessions per issue. Call 1-888-555-0142 at any hour.

## Managers

Managers should cover urgent work for the grieving employee and avoid contacting them about work during their leave. If the employee wants a gradual return, a reduced schedule for up to two weeks can be agreed without loss of pay.

## Regional differences

Mexico, France, and Brazil apply local legal minimums where they are more generous than this policy; see the regional HR pages.

documents.title: Sabbatical Program (HP-HR-112)
documents.text:
Sabbatical Program (HP-HR-112)

The sabbatical program rewards long service with an extended paid break for rest, study, or personal projects.

Who qualifies

5 years of continuous service at Harbor & Pine at the start of the sabbatical.
A performance rating of 3 ("Solid") or better in the most recent review cycle.
You may take one sabbatical per 5-year period of service.

Length and pay

6 weeks of fully paid leave, on top of normal vacation.
You may add up to 2 weeks of vacation directly before or after the sabbatical, for a maximum continuous absence of 8 weeks.
Benefits and equity vesting continue unchanged.

Applying

1. Discuss dates with your manager at least 4 months before the planned start.
2. Submit the sabbatical form in Compass under *Time Off > Sabbatical*, including a coverage plan for your responsibilities.
3. Your department head approves; People Operations confirms eligibility.

Restrictions

The sabbatical must start within 12 months of becoming eligible, or eligibility rolls into the next 5-year period.
Paid work for another employer during the sabbatical is not allowed. Volunteering, study, and travel are encouraged.
Sabbaticals cannot be paid out in cash and are not split into multiple shorter breaks.

After the sabbatical

You return to the same role and compensation. Many people share what they did at a Friday all-hands, but that is optional.

documents.title: Vacation and Paid Time Off (HP-HR-101)
documents.text:
# Vacation and Paid Time Off (HP-HR-101)

## Annual allowance

Full-time employees in the US and Canada receive **22 vacation days** per year. Vacation accrues monthly at **1.83 days per month**, starting on your first day.

After 5 years of service the allowance rises to 25 days.

## Carryover

You may carry over up to **5 unused days** into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by **March 31**; after that they expire. Vacation is paid out on termination where local law requires it.

## Booking time off

- Request vacation in Compass at least **2 weeks** ahead for absences longer than 3 days.
- Managers should respond within 3 working days.
- Engineers on the on-call rotation must arrange a swap before booking time off during their on-call week.

## Blackout periods

Warehouse and fulfilment staff cannot take vacation during the peak season blackout, from the **Monday before Thanksgiving through December 31**, except with written approval from the site manager. Office staff have no blackout period.

## Company holidays

Company holidays are not deducted from your vacation allowance. Office-specific holiday calendars are published by each regional office.

## Volunteer day

Each employee also gets one paid volunteer day per year, which does not count against vacation.

## Unpaid leave

Employees who have used their vacation may request up to 20 days of unpaid personal leave per year, subject to manager approval. Health benefits continue during unpaid leave of up to 30 days.

documents.title: Hybrid and Remote Work Policy
documents.text:
Hybrid and Remote Work Policy

Harbor & Pine operates a hybrid model for office-based teams. Warehouse roles are on-site by nature and are not covered by this policy.

Office attendance

Hybrid employees are expected in the office 3 days per week; Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days for every team.
Fully remote roles are approved case by case by the department head and People Operations.

Home office stipend

New hybrid and remote employees receive a one-time $600 home office stipend for a desk, chair, or monitor. Submit receipts in Ledgerly within 90 days of your start date. A further $200 refresh is available every 3 years.

Working from another location

You must normally work from a country where Harbor & Pine has a legal entity: the United States, Canada, Mexico, France, or Brazil.
Work from anywhere: you may work from another country for up to 20 working days per calendar year, with manager approval and a request filed at least 2 weeks in advance. Some countries are excluded for export-control reasons.
Working abroad longer than this can create tax and immigration obligations and needs People Operations approval.

Equipment and security

Use only your company laptop for work. Public Wi-Fi requires the company VPN. Restricted data must never be printed at home.

Core hours

Teams agree core collaboration hours, usually 10:00 to 15:00 local time.

documents.title: Performance Review Cycle
documents.text:
Harbor & Pine runs two performance review cycles each year, one in April and one in October. Both cycles are managed in Compass, our HR system, and follow the same steps.

The cycle opens with a self-review, which you have two weeks to complete. You describe your main contributions, the goals you set in the previous cycle, and where you want to grow. At the same time you can request feedback from up to five peers; peer feedback is optional but strongly encouraged for anyone working across teams.

Managers then write their review and propose a rating on the five-point scale: 1 Not meeting expectations, 2 Partially meeting, 3 Solid, 4 Strong, 5 Exceptional. Proposed ratings go through a calibration session within each department, where managers compare ratings to keep them fair and consistent. Ratings are not final until calibration is complete.

The October cycle is linked to compensation. Merit increases and bonus multipliers are decided from the calibrated October rating and take effect on February 1, the first day of the fiscal year. The April cycle is a development check-in and does not change pay, although promotions may be proposed in either cycle.

Employees who joined less than three months before a cycle closes are not rated in that cycle; they receive a written check-in instead. An employee who receives a rating of 1 is placed on a 60-day improvement plan agreed with their manager and People Operations.

You can appeal a final rating within ten working days by writing to your HR business partner.

documents.title: New Hire Onboarding Checklist
documents.text:
# New Hire Onboarding Checklist

This checklist is for managers and onboarding buddies preparing for a new team member.

## Before day 1

- Open an IT request at least **5 working days** before the start date so the laptop is imaged and shipped.
- Assign an onboarding buddy from the same team, but not the manager.
- Add the new hire to team calendars and chat channels.

## Day 1

- Laptop pickup and MFA enrolment with IT (about 45 minutes).
- Welcome session with People Operations at 10:00 local time.
- Lunch with the buddy, paid on the team card.

## First week

- Complete the mandatory security awareness and data classification training.
- Read the team handbook and set up a 1:1 schedule with the manager.
- Warehouse hires complete site safety induction before entering the floor.

## 30-60-90 plan

| Checkpoint | Focus |
|---|---|
| Day 30 | Tools, people, first small deliverable |
| Day 60 | Owns a recurring piece of work |
| Day 90 | Working independently; probation review |

The day-90 probation review is recorded in Compass. If it is not completed within 10 working days, probation is considered passed.

Engineering hires also ship a first change to production in their first two weeks, paired with their buddy.

## For remote hires

Remote employees receive their laptop by courier two working days before their start date and complete MFA enrolment on a video call with IT. The buddy should schedule at least two video coffees in the first week.

## Feedback on onboarding

At day 30, every new hire receives a short onboarding survey. Results are shared with People Operations and the hiring manager, and are used to update this checklist twice a year.

documents.title: Jury Duty and Civic Leave
documents.text:
Employees who are summoned for jury duty, called as a witness, or required to serve as an election poll worker are entitled to civic leave under this policy. Civic leave is separate from vacation, sick leave, and other leave types and does not reduce any of those balances.

Harbor & Pine pays your full base salary for up to ten working days of jury or witness service per calendar year. If service continues beyond ten days, the remaining days are unpaid unless local law requires otherwise; you may choose to use vacation instead. Any fee paid to you by the court may be kept.

Please send a copy of the summons to your manager and to People Operations as soon as you receive it, and record each day of service in Compass under Time Off, Civic. If you are released early on a given day and it is practical to work part of the shift, we ask you to check in with your manager, but you will not be penalised if you do not.

Employees serving as poll workers on an election day receive up to one paid day per election. Voting itself does not require a leave request: every employee may take up to two paid hours to vote if their shift does not leave enough time outside working hours.

Military reservists should refer to the separate military leave policy, which provides different protections. Managers may never discourage an employee from performing civic duties or retaliate against anyone who does.

documents.title: Employee Referral Program
documents.text:
# Employee Referral Program

Great people know great people. When you refer a candidate who is hired, you receive a referral bonus.

## Bonus amounts

| Role family | Bonus |
|---|---|
| Engineering, data, and security | $3,000 |
| All other salaried roles | $1,500 |
| Warehouse hourly roles | $500 |

The bonus is paid in the payroll after the new hire completes **90 days** of employment, and is subject to normal tax withholding.

## How to refer

1. Submit the candidate in the Careers portal under *Refer a friend* before they apply themselves.
2. Add a short note about how you know them.
3. Recruiting will keep you informed of the outcome, but cannot share interview feedback.

## Rules

- Managers and recruiters cannot receive a bonus for roles they hire for.
- Referrals of former employees count only if they left more than 12 months ago.
- If two employees refer the same candidate, the earliest submission wins.
- Executive roles (VP and above) are excluded.

## Referral events

Twice a year Recruiting runs a referral month with a doubled bonus for hard-to-fill roles; watch the #careers channel for announcements.

## Tax and payment details

The bonus is added to your regular payslip as a separate line called "Referral award" and is taxed as supplemental income. If you leave the company before the 90-day mark of the person you referred, the bonus is still paid, provided you are employed on the date the new hire reaches 90 days.

## Diversity sourcing

Recruiting especially welcomes referrals from communities that are under-represented in logistics and engineering. Referral bonuses are the same for every candidate; the program never pays more based on a candidate's background.

documents.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy (FIN-EXP-2)
documents.text:
# Expense Reimbursement Policy (FIN-EXP-2)

This policy covers everyday business expenses that are not travel. Travel, lodging, and per-diem rules are in the separate Travel Policy (FIN-TRV-1).

## Submitting expenses

- Submit every expense in **Ledgerly** within **30 days** of the purchase. Claims older than 90 days are rejected.
- Attach an itemised receipt for any expense of **$25 or more**.
- Reimbursements are paid with the next payroll after approval.

## Common categories and limits

| Category | Limit |
|---|---|
| Client entertainment | $120 per attendee, including alcohol |
| Team meals (manager-approved) | $45 per person |
| Books and online courses | $500 per year without pre-approval |
| Conference tickets | Pre-approval by manager required |
| Software subscriptions | Must go through IT procurement, not expenses |

## Approvals

- Your manager approves all claims.
- Any single claim over **$1,000** also needs approval from a vice president.
- Alcohol is only reimbursable when a client is present.

## Not reimbursable

Personal grooming, fines and parking tickets, gifts above $75 per recipient, and home internet (covered by the remote work stipend instead).

Questions go to expenses@harborpine.example.

## Expenses in foreign currencies

Submit foreign-currency receipts in the original currency; Ledgerly converts them using the exchange rate on the transaction date. If you paid with a personal card, you may instead submit your card statement rate.

## Missing receipts

If a receipt is lost, complete a missing-receipt declaration in Ledgerly. Each employee may use no more than three missing-receipt declarations per year, and never for amounts over $250.

documents.title: Travel Policy and Per Diem (FIN-TRV-1)
documents.text:
# Travel Policy and Per Diem (FIN-TRV-1)

All business travel is booked through the company travel desk, TideTravel, so we can locate you in an emergency.

## Flights

- Economy class for flights under **6 hours**.
- Premium economy for flights of 6 hours or more.
- Business class only for flights over **10 hours**, with vice-president approval.
- Book at least 14 days ahead where possible.

## Hotels

The nightly cap is **$250** in US and Canadian cities and $325 in New York, San Francisco, and Toronto. International caps follow the per-diem table below.

## Per diem for meals and incidentals

You receive a flat daily allowance instead of submitting meal receipts. Domestic per diem is **$68 per day**. On travel days you receive 75% of the daily rate.

| City | Daily per diem | Hotel cap |
|---|---|---|
| London | GBP 85 | GBP 230 |
| Paris | EUR 80 | EUR 220 |
| Mexico City | USD 55 | USD 180 |
| São Paulo | USD 60 | USD 190 |

## Ground transport

Use public transport or ride-hailing; rental cars need manager approval. Personal car use is covered by the mileage policy.

## Claiming

Record per diem and lodging in Ledgerly within 30 days of returning.

## Travel safety

TideTravel tracks bookings and contacts travellers during emergencies such as natural disasters or political unrest. Travel to countries rated high-risk by our security provider requires approval from the Chief Operating Officer and a pre-trip briefing.

## Changes and cancellations

Prefer flexible fares when plans are uncertain. Change fees caused by business reasons are reimbursed; fees caused by personal reasons are not. Unused non-refundable tickets are recorded as credits by TideTravel and must be used for your next trip.

## Combining business and personal travel

You may extend a business trip for personal days if the extra cost to the company is zero. Any additional hotel nights or fare differences are paid by you directly.

documents.title: Corporate Card (Harbor Card) Guidelines
documents.text:
# Corporate Card (Harbor Card) Guidelines

The Harbor Card is a company-liability charge card issued to employees who travel or buy regularly for the business.

## Who gets a card

Managers, anyone who travels more than four times a year, and roles nominated by a department head. Request one through the Finance portal.

## Limits

| Cardholder | Monthly limit |
|---|---|
| Standard employee | $5,000 |
| Manager and above | $15,000 |
| Temporary increase | Up to $25,000 for 30 days, with Finance approval |

## Rules of use

- Business expenses only. **No personal purchases**, even if you intend to repay them.
- **Cash withdrawals are not allowed**; ATM attempts are blocked.
- Transactions sync to Ledgerly automatically; you must add a receipt and category within **10 days**.
- Unreconciled transactions older than 45 days lead to the card being suspended.

## Lost or stolen card

Call the card issuer immediately on **1-800-555-0199** (24 hours), then notify cards@harborpine.example. A replacement arrives in 3 to 5 working days.

## Leaving the company

Cards are cancelled on your last day. Outstanding transactions must be reconciled before your final paycheck is processed.

## Travel and foreign transactions

The Harbor Card has no foreign transaction fees. Notify Finance before long trips to countries where you have not used the card before, to avoid fraud blocks.

## Declined transactions

If a payment is declined, check the Finance portal for the reason. Merchant categories such as gambling, jewellery, and cash-equivalent services are always blocked. Ask Finance to unblock a category for a specific business purchase; approval is usually given within one working day.

documents.title: Invoice Approval Thresholds (FIN-AP-3)
documents.text:
# Invoice Approval Thresholds (FIN-AP-3)

Accounts Payable pays supplier invoices only after they are approved at the right level. Thresholds apply to the **total invoice value** before tax.

## Approval matrix

| Invoice amount | Required approver |
|---|---|
| Under $5,000 | Budget-owning manager |
| $5,000 to $24,999 | Director |
| $25,000 to $99,999 | Vice President of Finance |
| $100,000 and above | Chief Financial Officer plus a second executive signature |

Splitting one purchase into several invoices to stay under a threshold is a policy violation.

## Three-way match

Every invoice above $5,000 must match a purchase order and a goods-received or service-confirmation record. Mismatches over **2%** of the PO value are returned to the requester.

## Payment terms

Standard terms are **net 45**. Early-payment discounts are taken when offered. Invoices must reference a valid vendor ID (format V-12345); unknown vendors go through vendor onboarding first.

## Where to send invoices

Suppliers email invoices to ap@harborpine.example. Invoices sent directly to employees are delayed. Approvals happen in Ledgerly, and approvers receive a reminder after 3 days.

## Recurring invoices

For recurring services such as cloud hosting or carrier contracts, the approval level is based on the **annual** contract value, and approval is given once when the contract is signed. Monthly invoices within 5% of the contracted amount are then paid without further approval.

## Disputed invoices

If you disagree with an invoice, mark it as disputed in Ledgerly within 10 days. Accounts Payable informs the supplier and pauses the payment clock. Never ask a supplier to resend an invoice with a lower amount to fit an approval level.

documents.title: Purchase Orders and Vendor Onboarding
documents.text:
Before Harbor & Pine can buy from a new supplier, the supplier must be onboarded by Procurement. Onboarding protects us from fraud, ensures we pay taxes correctly, and checks that suppliers who touch our data meet our security standards.

To request a new vendor, the requesting employee opens a Vendor Request in the Finance portal with the supplier's legal name, contact, and a short description of what we are buying. Procurement then collects a tax form (a W-9 for US suppliers or a W-8BEN-E for foreign suppliers), bank details verified by a call-back to a known phone number, and a certificate of insurance where relevant. When onboarding is complete the supplier receives a vendor ID in the format V followed by five digits, for example V-20417.

Any supplier that will process, store, or access Confidential or Restricted data must also pass a security review before a contract is signed. Security reviews take about ten working days and include a questionnaire and, for higher-risk vendors, evidence such as a SOC 2 report.

Purchase orders are required for any purchase of $5,000 or more, and for all recurring services regardless of amount. The PO is raised in Ledgerly against a budget line and approved according to the same approval levels used for invoices. Suppliers should quote the PO number on every invoice.

Bank detail changes requested by a supplier are always verified by phone, never by email alone, because invoice redirection fraud is one of the most common attacks against finance teams.

documents.title: Mileage Reimbursement
documents.text:
# Mileage Reimbursement

When you use your personal vehicle for business, Harbor & Pine reimburses you per mile instead of paying fuel receipts.

## Rate

- **$0.67 per mile** in the US, updated each January to match the federal standard rate.
- **CAD 0.70 per kilometre** in Canada.

The rate covers fuel, wear, insurance, and depreciation, so fuel, tolls covered by the rate, and car washes are not claimed separately. Parking and bridge tolls **are** claimable with receipts.

## What counts as business mileage

- Driving between two work locations, for example from the Portland office to the Reno distribution centre.
- Driving to a client or supplier site.
- **Your normal commute is excluded.** If you drive from home straight to a client, claim only the distance that exceeds your usual commute.

## How to claim

1. Log each trip in Ledgerly using the mileage tool, which calculates the distance from the start and end addresses.
2. Add the business purpose.
3. Submit monthly, no later than 30 days after the month ends.

## Insurance

Your personal policy must include business-use cover. Harbor & Pine does not cover deductibles for accidents in personal vehicles. Rental cars for longer trips are covered by the travel policy instead.

## Electric vehicles

Employees using a personal electric vehicle claim the same per-mile rate. Charging at a company site is free and cannot be claimed separately; charging at a public station during a business trip is already covered by the mileage rate.

documents.title: Payroll Calendar and Pay Dates
documents.text:
# Payroll Calendar and Pay Dates

## Pay frequency

US and Canadian employees are paid **semi-monthly**: on the **15th** and on the **last business day** of each month. If the 15th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, pay is issued on the preceding business day.

Hourly warehouse staff are paid **bi-weekly** on Fridays, based on timesheets approved by the shift lead.

## Payroll cut-off

Changes that affect pay must reach Payroll **5 business days** before the pay date. This includes:

- New hires and terminations
- Bank account changes
- Salary changes and one-time bonuses
- Approved expense reimbursements

Changes received after the cut-off are processed in the following cycle.

## Payslips

Payslips are available in Compass on the pay date. Year-end tax forms (W-2 and T4) are published by January 31.

## Errors and off-cycle payments

If you are underpaid by more than $200 because of a payroll error, Payroll will issue an off-cycle payment within 3 business days. Smaller corrections are made in the next regular payroll. Report problems to payroll@harborpine.example.

## Final pay

Employees who resign receive their final pay on the next regular pay date. Employees whose employment is ended by the company are paid within the time required by state or provincial law, which can be the same day. Final pay includes unused vacation where required, approved but unpaid expenses, and any pro-rated bonus the bonus plan allows.

## Direct deposit

Pay is only made by direct deposit. You can split your net pay across up to three bank accounts in Compass. A new bank account takes effect from the first payroll after the cut-off, and the first deposit to a new account is preceded by a one-cent verification transfer.

documents.title: Fiscal Year and Annual Budget Planning
documents.text:
Harbor & Pine's fiscal year runs from February 1 to January 31. Fiscal years are named after the calendar year in which they end, so FY2027 runs from February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027. Quarters therefore close at the end of April, July, October, and January.

Annual budget planning starts in September. Finance publishes top-down targets for revenue and operating expenses in the first week of September, and each department head submits a bottom-up budget, including headcount, by October 15. Budget reviews with the executive team take place in November.

The budget is locked in mid-December. After the lock, new headcount or spending outside the approved budget requires a formal reforecast request. Reforecasts are reviewed quarterly, so a request submitted in March is considered at the end of the first quarter.

Unspent budget does not roll over from one fiscal year to the next. Departments that expect to underspend are asked to tell Finance by the end of the third quarter so funds can be reallocated.

Capital expenditures, such as warehouse racking, forklifts, and servers, are planned separately in a capital plan with a threshold of $10,000 per item. Anything below that threshold is treated as an operating expense.

Questions about budget ownership or cost centres should go to your finance business partner, listed on the Finance intranet page.

documents.title: Runbook: Deploying tidewater-api to Production
documents.text:
# Runbook: Deploying tidewater-api to Production

tidewater-api is the customer-facing REST API behind the Tidewater shipping platform. All production deploys go through the **shipyard** CLI.

## Deploy windows

- Monday to Thursday, **09:00 to 16:00 Pacific**.
- No deploys on Fridays, weekends, or company holidays without an approved exception from the engineering director.
- The annual change freeze runs from the Monday before Thanksgiving to January 2.

## Pre-flight

1. The release build is green in CI and tagged, e.g. `tw-2026.10.3`.
2. Database migrations in the release have been applied to staging (sandbar) and are backward compatible.
3. Announce the deploy in #deploys with the release tag and a link to the changelog.

## Deploy

```
shipyard deploy tidewater-api --env prod --release tw-2026.10.3
```

shipyard starts a **canary at 5% of traffic for 20 minutes**. During the canary, watch the tidewater-api dashboard: error rate must stay below 0.5% and p95 latency below 400 ms.

## Promote

If the canary is healthy, shipyard promotes automatically to 25%, then 100%, over a further 15 minutes. You can promote manually with `shipyard promote tidewater-api`.

## If something looks wrong

Stop the rollout with `shipyard pause tidewater-api` and follow the tidewater-api rollback runbook. Never hot-patch production containers.

documents.title: Runbook: Rolling Back tidewater-api
documents.text:
# Runbook: Rolling Back tidewater-api

Use this runbook when a tidewater-api release causes errors, latency regression, or incorrect data. It does **not** apply to pinecone-router, which has its own configuration rollback procedure.

## Decide quickly

Roll back first and debug later. If the error rate exceeds 2% for 5 minutes after a deploy, or any SEV2 or higher incident is linked to the release, roll back.

## Steps

1. Find the last good release: `shipyard releases tidewater-api --limit 5`.
2. Run the rollback:
   ```
   shipyard rollback tidewater-api --to tw-2026.10.2
   ```
3. shipyard shifts 100% of traffic to the previous release in one step; there is no canary on rollback. It normally completes in under **4 minutes**.
4. Confirm the error rate is back to baseline on the dashboard.
5. Post in #deploys and in the incident channel, if one is open.

## Database migrations

Rollback only reverts application code. Because all migrations must be backward compatible, the previous release runs against the new schema. **Never run a down-migration in production** without the database on-call engineer.

## Feature flags

If the problem is isolated to a flagged feature, turning the flag off in Beacon is faster than a full rollback. Do that first, then decide whether a rollback is still needed.

## Target

The rollback should be complete within **15 minutes** of the decision.

documents.title: Runbook: pinecone-router Configuration Rollback
documents.text:
# Runbook: pinecone-router Configuration Rollback

pinecone-router is deployed from configuration "generations", not from shipyard releases. Most pinecone-router incidents come from a bad routing configuration, so rolling back means reverting to an earlier configuration generation. **Do not use shipyard rollback for pinecone-router.**

## When to roll back

- Carrier requests are being routed to the wrong carrier or region.
- Timeouts to carriers jump after a configuration push.
- The router health check shows `config_valid=false`.

## Steps

1. List recent generations:
   ```
   routerctl config history --last 10
   ```
2. **Drain** traffic from the affected region so in-flight requests finish: `routerctl drain --region us-west`.
3. Revert:
   ```
   routerctl config revert --generation 412
   ```
4. Wait for every router node to report the new generation (usually about **4 minutes**, because nodes reload in batches of 10).
5. Undrain: `routerctl undrain --region us-west`.

## Things to know

- A revert creates a **new** generation number that copies the old one, so history is never rewritten.
- Rolling back pinecone-router does not touch tidewater-api; if both changed together, roll back the router first.
- Reverts require two people: the on-call engineer runs the command and a second engineer confirms the generation number in the incident channel.

documents.title: Incident Severity Levels
documents.text:
# Incident Severity Levels

Every production incident gets a severity at declaration. Severity decides who is paged, how fast we communicate, and whether a postmortem is required. When unsure, pick the higher severity; it can be downgraded later.

| Severity | Definition | Response |
|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Full outage of Tidewater, data loss, or a security breach affecting customers | Page incident commander within **5 minutes**; status page update within **15 minutes**; updates every 30 minutes |
| SEV2 | Major feature unavailable or severe degradation for many customers, e.g. label printing failing | Page on-call and incident commander; status page within 30 minutes; updates hourly |
| SEV3 | Partial degradation with a workaround, or a single enterprise customer affected | On-call handles during business hours; no status page by default |
| SEV4 | Minor bug or cosmetic issue with no customer impact | Ticket in the team backlog |

## Roles

- **Incident commander (IC):** owns decisions and coordination, not debugging.
- **Communications lead:** writes status page and customer updates.
- **Subject-matter responders:** fix the problem.

## After the incident

SEV1 and SEV2 incidents require a written postmortem; see the postmortem process document. SEV3 incidents need a short summary in the incident ticket.

Warehouse operational problems, such as a conveyor failure, use the warehouse incident process, not these software severity levels.

documents.title: Engineering On-Call Policy
documents.text:
Engineering On-Call Policy

Rotation

Each service team runs a weekly rotation with a primary and a secondary.
Handoff happens every Tuesday at 10:00 Pacific during a 15-minute handoff meeting.
Engineers join the rotation after 3 months at the company and after shadowing one full week.

Expectations

Acknowledge a page within 10 minutes, day or night.
If the primary does not acknowledge within 15 minutes, the page escalates to the secondary, and after 30 minutes to the engineering manager.
Carry your laptop and have reliable internet during your on-call week.

Compensation

An on-call stipend of $400 per week for the primary and $200 for the secondary, paid in the next payroll.
If you are paged and work on an incident after 2:00 a.m. local time, you may take the next working day off as a compensatory day. Record it in Compass as *Comp day*.

Swaps

Swap shifts in PagerTide and tell your manager. Before booking vacation during your on-call week, find a swap.

Health of the rotation

Teams review page volume monthly. If a rotation averages more than 2 out-of-hours pages per week over a month, the team must dedicate time in the next sprint to reduce alert noise.

Escalation contacts

Every team keeps its escalation path in PagerTide. During a SEV1 the incident commander can page any team directly, including teams outside their own on-call rotation, and may page the engineering director if no responder acknowledges within 30 minutes.

documents.title: Runbook: ledger-db Database Failover
documents.text:
# Runbook: ledger-db Database Failover

ledger-db is the PostgreSQL cluster that stores billing, invoices, and shipment charges for Tidewater. The primary runs in **us-east-2**; a streaming replica runs in **us-west-2**.

## Objectives

- **RPO:** 30 seconds (maximum acceptable data loss).
- **RTO:** 10 minutes (time to restore writes).

## When to fail over

Only when the primary is unavailable or unrecoverable for more than 5 minutes, and only with explicit approval from the **incident commander** of a declared SEV1 or SEV2. Failover is never used to fix slow queries.

## Steps

1. Confirm replication lag on the replica is below 30 seconds: `pgctl lag ledger-db-replica`.
2. Fence the old primary so it cannot accept writes: `pgctl fence ledger-db-primary`.
3. Promote the replica:
   ```
   pgctl promote ledger-db-replica
   ```
4. Update the service endpoint: `pgctl dns switch ledger-db --to us-west-2`. tidewater-api reconnects automatically within about 60 seconds.
5. Verify writes by creating a test invoice in the internal admin tool.

## After failover

- The cluster runs without a replica until a new one is built from the promoted primary; this takes about 2 hours.
- **Fail back** to us-east-2 only during a planned maintenance window, never during the incident.
- Record the exact promotion time in the incident ticket for the postmortem.

documents.title: Error ERR-4471: Manifest Checksum Mismatch
documents.text:
# Error ERR-4471: Manifest Checksum Mismatch

## Symptom

tidewater-api returns HTTP 409 with error code **ERR-4471** and the message `manifest checksum mismatch` when a customer submits or updates a shipment manifest. Customers usually see it as "Your manifest could not be saved, please retry".

## Cause

The checksum that tidewater-api computes for the manifest does not match the checksum cached by **pinecone-router** for the same manifest ID. In almost every case the router is serving a **stale manifest cache entry**, typically after a manifest was edited twice within a few seconds or after a router node restarted mid-write.

## Diagnosis

1. Look up the manifest ID in the error log entry.
2. Compare checksums: `routerctl cache get manifest:<manifest-id>` versus the value in the tidewater-api admin tool.
3. If more than 50 ERR-4471 errors occur in 10 minutes, treat it as a SEV3 and check for a router node restart loop.

## Fix

Purge the cache key for the affected manifest:

```
routerctl cache purge manifest:<manifest-id>
```

The customer can then resubmit. For bulk occurrences, purge by customer prefix with `routerctl cache purge --prefix manifest:<customer-id>`.

## Do not

Do not roll back tidewater-api for ERR-4471; the API is behaving correctly by rejecting inconsistent data.

documents.title: Error ERR-5120: Token Issuer Mismatch
documents.text:
# Error ERR-5120: Token Issuer Mismatch

## Symptom

Requests fail with HTTP 401 and error code **ERR-5120** (`token issuer mismatch`). Internal services that call each other with service tokens are most affected; customer API keys are rarely involved.

## Background

Service tokens are issued by **keel-auth**, the internal identity service. Each token carries an issuer claim and an issue timestamp. Receiving services reject a token if the issuer is not the expected keel-auth environment, or if the timestamp is more than **90 seconds** in the future relative to their own clock.

## Common causes

1. **Clock skew.** A host whose clock has drifted more than 90 seconds. This is the cause in roughly 80% of cases, usually on a freshly provisioned node where NTP did not start.
2. **Wrong environment.** A staging service configured with the production keel-auth URL, or the reverse, after a configuration copy.
3. **Issuer rotation.** During the yearly issuer-key rotation, services that have not reloaded keys reject new tokens for up to 10 minutes.

## Fix

- Check the clock: `timedatectl status`. If NTP is inactive, run `sudo systemctl restart chronyd` and confirm the offset is below 1 second.
- Verify the `KEEL_AUTH_ISSUER` value in the service config matches the environment.
- During rotation, restart the affected service to reload issuer keys.

ERR-5120 is not a customer password or MFA problem; do not reset user credentials for it.

documents.title: Error ERR-3308: API Rate Limit Exceeded
documents.text:
# Error ERR-3308: API Rate Limit Exceeded

## What it means

tidewater-api returns HTTP 429 with error code **ERR-3308** when an API key exceeds its request rate limit. The response includes a `Retry-After` header with the number of seconds to wait.

## Limits by plan

| Plan | Requests per minute per API key | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | 120 | 20 |
| Growth | 600 | 100 |
| Enterprise | 3,000 (negotiable) | 500 |

Limits are applied per API key, not per customer account, so customers with several keys share nothing between them.

## How customers should handle it

- Respect `Retry-After` and use exponential backoff with jitter.
- Batch shipment creation with the `/v2/shipments:batch` endpoint (up to 100 shipments per call) instead of one call per shipment.
- Use webhooks rather than polling tracking endpoints.

## Support guidance

If an Enterprise customer is repeatedly limited during legitimate peaks, support can open a request for a temporary limit increase; the platform team approves increases up to 2x for 30 days. Growth and Starter customers should be pointed to an upgrade.

ERR-3308 is never caused by our infrastructure being down; if you see 5xx errors as well, check the status page and the incident channel.

documents.title: pinecone-router Architecture Overview
documents.text:
pinecone-router is the internal service that decides which carrier and which carrier endpoint handle each shipment request. tidewater-api calls pinecone-router for every rate quote, label purchase, and tracking lookup; pinecone-router in turn talks to more than forty carrier APIs.

The router runs as a fleet of stateless nodes in three regions: us-east, us-west, and eu-central. Each node holds the full routing configuration in memory. Configuration is versioned as numbered generations; a generation contains the carrier priority lists, per-carrier timeouts, region preferences, and circuit-breaker thresholds. Generations are pushed by the platform team through a reviewed pull request and applied to nodes in batches of ten.

Each carrier connection has a circuit breaker. If more than 20 percent of requests to a carrier fail within one minute, the breaker opens for 60 seconds and requests fall back to the next carrier on the priority list, if the customer's contract allows fallback. Breaker state is visible on the router dashboard.

pinecone-router also maintains a short-lived cache of shipment manifests and rate quotes, with a time-to-live of 15 minutes for quotes and 24 hours for manifests. This cache reduces load on tidewater-api's database but is the source of some consistency errors when manifests are edited quickly.

The service is owned by the Routing team. Its on-call rotation is separate from the tidewater-api rotation, and incidents that involve both services should page both. Capacity planning assumes a peak of 8,000 requests per second during the November and December season.

documents.title: Feature Flags with Beacon
documents.text:
Feature Flags with Beacon

Beacon is our feature flag service. Use it to release changes gradually, run experiments, and switch off risky features without a deploy.

Naming

Flags are named <team>.<feature>.<purpose>, for example routing.multi-carrier-fallback.release. Purpose is one of release, experiment, ops (kill switch), or permission.

Creating a flag

1. Create the flag in the Beacon console with an owner and a planned removal date.
2. Default it to off in production.
3. Reference it in code through the Beacon SDK; never read flags from environment variables.

Rolling out

Start with internal accounts, then 1%, 10%, 50%, and 100% of customers.
Each step should run at least 24 hours for customer-facing changes.
Changes to flags in production are logged and announced automatically in #flags.

Cleanup

Release flags must be removed within 60 days of reaching 100%. Beacon opens a cleanup ticket automatically on day 45. Teams with more than 25 stale flags cannot create new release flags until they clean up.

Kill switches

Ops flags are permanent and are expected to be used during incidents. Switching off an ops flag is always faster than rolling back a deploy.

Experiments

Experiment flags assign customers to variants at random with a stable hash of the account ID, so a customer always sees the same variant. Experiments need a written hypothesis and a success metric before starting, and the analytics team reviews results after at least two weeks.

Permissions flags

Permission flags enable features for specific customers, for example a beta feature for one Enterprise account. They are owned by Product, not engineering, and are reviewed every quarter.

documents.title: Code Review Policy
documents.text:
# Code Review Policy

All production code at Harbor & Pine is reviewed before merge.

## Approvals

- **One approval** from a team member is required for most repositories.
- **Two approvals** are required for the tidewater-api `payments` and `billing` modules, for pinecone-router configuration, and for anything touching keel-auth.
- Authors cannot approve their own pull requests, and a reviewer who pair-programmed the change does not count as an independent approver.

## Size

Keep pull requests under **400 changed lines** excluding generated files and tests. Larger changes should be split or behind a feature flag.

## Turnaround

Reviewers should respond within **one working day**. If a review is blocking an incident fix, ask in the team channel and expect a response within an hour.

## What reviewers look for

- Correctness and tests for new behaviour
- Backward-compatible database migrations
- No secrets, tokens, or customer data in code or logs
- Clear naming and a useful description

## Emergency changes

During a SEV1 or SEV2, a fix may be merged with one approval from any senior engineer, even in modules that normally need two. A follow-up review must happen within two working days.

## Automated checks

Every pull request must pass unit tests, linting, the dependency vulnerability scan, and the secrets scanner before merge. A reviewer may not approve a pull request with failing required checks, even if the failures look unrelated.

## Ownership

Each repository has a CODEOWNERS file. The code owner team must be one of the approvers. For shared libraries, changes require approval from the platform team in addition to the team making the change.

documents.title: Postmortem Process
documents.text:
Every SEV1 and SEV2 incident must have a written postmortem. The goal is to learn and prevent recurrence, not to assign blame. Postmortems are blameless: they describe what people did and why it made sense at the time, and they focus on gaps in systems, tooling, and process.

The incident commander assigns a postmortem owner before the incident is closed. The owner drafts the document using the standard template within five business days of the incident's resolution. The template asks for a summary, customer impact with numbers, a timeline in UTC, root cause and contributing factors, what went well, what went poorly, and action items.

A postmortem review meeting is held within ten business days. The responders, the owning team's manager, and anyone else who wants to learn are invited. The meeting reviews the timeline, challenges the root cause analysis, and agrees action items. Each action item has an owner and a due date and is tracked as a ticket with the label postmortem.

Action items classified as critical must be completed within thirty days. Engineering leadership reviews overdue postmortem actions in the monthly operations review.

Completed postmortems are published in the engineering wiki and are readable by all employees. Customer-facing summaries for SEV1 incidents are written by the communications lead and sent to affected Enterprise customers within five business days, as required by our SLA commitments.

documents.title: Runbook: driftwood Consumer Lag
documents.text:
# Runbook: driftwood Consumer Lag

driftwood is the internal event bus (Kafka-based) that carries shipment status events from carriers to tidewater-api, notifications, and analytics.

## Alert

The alert **driftwood-consumer-lag-high** fires when any consumer group is more than **50,000 messages** behind on a topic for 10 minutes. The most important group is `tidewater-tracking`, because lag there delays tracking updates that customers see.

## Diagnose

1. Open the driftwood dashboard and find the lagging group and partitions.
2. Check whether lag is growing on **all partitions** (consumers too slow or down) or on **one partition** (a poison message or a hot key).
3. Check consumer logs for repeated deserialisation errors.

## Fix

- **Consumers down or slow:** scale the consumer deployment, e.g. `kubectl scale deploy tidewater-tracking-consumer --replicas=12`. Do not exceed the partition count (24), since extra consumers sit idle.
- **Poison message:** move the offending message to the dead-letter topic with `driftwood dlq move --group tidewater-tracking --partition 7 --offset <offset>`.
- **Hot key:** escalate to the Routing team; a single carrier is often flooding events.

## Customer impact

Lag above 200,000 messages on `tidewater-tracking` means tracking pages are more than about 15 minutes stale. Declare a SEV3 and inform support so they can use the tracking-delay macro.

documents.title: Secrets Management with Vault
documents.text:
Secrets Management with Vault

Application secrets, such as database passwords, carrier API keys, and signing keys, are stored in HashiCorp Vault. They must never be stored in code, configuration files committed to Git, chat, or tickets.

Paths

Secrets live under secret/<environment>/<service>/<name>, for example secret/prod/tidewater-api/ledger-db-password. Each service has a Vault role that can read only its own path.

Accessing secrets

Services read secrets at start-up using their Kubernetes service account.
Engineers can read production secrets only through a break-glass request approved by a second engineer, which is logged and expires after 1 hour.

Rotation

Service credentials (database users, internal tokens) rotate automatically every 90 days.
Carrier API keys rotate when the carrier allows it, at least yearly.
Any secret that may have been exposed, for example pasted into a chat, must be rotated within 24 hours, and the exposure reported to security@harborpine.example.

This policy covers machine secrets only. Rules for employee login passwords and MFA are in the separate password and MFA policies.

Detection

A pre-commit hook and a CI scanner block commits that contain strings looking like keys. If the scanner flags a false positive, add it to the allowlist through a reviewed change rather than disabling the hook.

documents.title: Staging Environment (sandbar)
documents.text:
sandbar is the shared staging environment for Tidewater. It runs the same services as production, including tidewater-api, pinecone-router, keel-auth, and driftwood, but at a smaller scale and in a single region, us-east.

Every merge to the main branch of a service is deployed to sandbar automatically within about ten minutes. Release candidates for production must have run in sandbar for at least two hours, and any database migration must be applied in sandbar first.

sandbar's data is refreshed from production every Sunday at 02:00 Pacific. During the refresh, which takes about three hours, sandbar is unavailable. All personal data is masked during the refresh: names, email addresses, phone numbers and street addresses are replaced with synthetic values, and payment details are removed entirely. Because of masking, sandbar data is classified as Internal rather than Restricted. Never copy unmasked production data into sandbar or into a developer laptop.

Carrier integrations in sandbar point at carrier sandboxes where available. Labels created in sandbar are not valid and are watermarked VOID. A few carriers have no sandbox; for them pinecone-router returns canned responses.

Teams that need an isolated environment for a risky change can create a short-lived preview environment from the developer portal. Preview environments are deleted automatically after 72 hours and use only synthetic data.

Problems with sandbar should be reported in the platform-support channel. sandbar outages are never declared as incidents, but the platform team aims to fix blocking issues within one working day.

documents.title: Password Policy (SEC-PW-1)
documents.text:
# Password Policy (SEC-PW-1)

This policy applies to employee passwords for single sign-on (SSO), laptops, and any system not yet behind SSO.

## Requirements

- Minimum length of **14 characters**. Passphrases of four or more random words are encouraged.
- No complexity rules beyond length; we check new passwords against a list of known breached passwords instead.
- Never reuse a work password on any other site.

## Rotation

- **Standard accounts:** no scheduled rotation. You change your password only when there is a reason to believe it may be compromised, or when Security asks you to.
- **Privileged administrator accounts** (production cloud consoles, domain admins, Vault operators): rotate every **180 days**.
- **Shared break-glass accounts:** rotated after every use.

## Password manager

Every employee has a company licence for **Keyring**, our password manager. Store all work credentials there. Sharing credentials is only allowed through Keyring shared folders, never by chat or email.

## If you suspect compromise

Change the password immediately from the SSO portal, then report it to security@harborpine.example or call the security hotline at extension **4400**.

## Lockout

Ten failed login attempts lock the account for 15 minutes. The IT service desk can unlock it after verifying your identity.

documents.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Standard
documents.text:
# Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Standard

Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for every Harbor & Pine account that supports it, starting with single sign-on.

## Allowed factors

| Factor | Allowed for |
|---|---|
| Hardware security key (FIDO2) | Everyone; **required** for administrators and finance approvers |
| Authenticator app push with number matching | All employees |
| Authenticator app one-time code | All employees |
| SMS codes | Not allowed, except for warehouse shared kiosks |

## Enrolment

New hires enrol two factors on day 1 with IT: usually the authenticator app and a hardware key. Download and store your **10 backup codes** in Keyring.

## Lost or replaced phone or key

1. Use a backup code or your second factor to sign in.
2. Remove the lost factor from the SSO portal under *Security > Devices*.
3. If you have no working factor, contact the IT service desk. They reset MFA only after a **live video call** where you show your badge or government ID. Resets are never done over email or by a colleague on your behalf.

## Push fatigue

If you receive an MFA prompt you did not start, **deny it** and report it to security@harborpine.example immediately. Unexpected prompts often mean your password has been stolen.

## Service accounts

Machine accounts cannot use MFA and must instead authenticate with short-lived credentials from Vault.

documents.title: Data Classification Standard (SEC-DC-2)
documents.text:
# Data Classification Standard (SEC-DC-2)

All information at Harbor & Pine belongs to one of four classes. The class decides where data may be stored and how it can be shared.

| Class | Examples | Key handling rules |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Marketing site, published pricing, press releases | No restrictions |
| Internal | Policies, org charts, masked staging data | Share inside the company only |
| Confidential | Contracts, financial forecasts, source code, customer shipment volumes | Need-to-know; encrypted in transit; external sharing needs an NDA |
| Restricted | Customer personal data, payroll, health information, credentials, payment card data | Strictly limited access; encrypted at rest; **never on personal devices**; logged access |

## Labelling

Documents in the company drive must carry a label. Unlabelled documents are treated as Confidential.

## Email and sharing

- Restricted data may only be emailed outside the company using the **encrypted mail** option (add [secure] to the subject line).
- Do not paste Confidential or Restricted data into external AI tools or translation websites.
- Use approved company drives; personal cloud storage is blocked.

## Printing and disposal

Restricted documents may be printed only on secure-release printers in the office. Paper is destroyed in the locked shredding bins.

## Incidents

Suspected exposure of Confidential or Restricted data must be reported to Security within 1 hour.

documents.title: Lost or Stolen Laptop Procedure
documents.text:
# Lost or Stolen Laptop Procedure

Company laptops hold sensitive data. A fast report lets us protect it, so you will never be penalised for reporting a loss.

## Within 1 hour

1. Report the loss to the Security team: email security@harborpine.example **and** call the security hotline at **extension 4400** (or +1-503-555-4400 from outside the office), available 24/7.
2. Tell them when and where you last had the device, and whether it was powered off or asleep.

Security will lock the device and send a **remote wipe** command through Anchor MDM. Laptops are fully disk-encrypted, so a powered-off device is low risk, but we still wipe it.

## Within 48 hours

- If the laptop was stolen, file a **police report** and send the report number to Security.
- Change your SSO password from another device, and review recent sign-ins in the SSO portal.

## Replacement

IT ships a replacement within **2 business days**. Your files are restored from the company cloud drive; anything stored only locally is lost.

## Phones and other devices

Lost company phones and hardware security keys follow the same reporting rule. For a lost MFA key, see the MFA standard.

## Found it again?

Do not power it on. Return it to IT so it can be inspected and re-imaged.

## Travelling with a laptop

Never check a laptop into airline hold luggage, and do not leave it visible in a parked car. When crossing borders, you may be asked to unlock devices; contact Security before travelling to countries listed on the travel risk page so they can issue a clean travel laptop if needed.

documents.title: Phishing Awareness and Reporting
documents.text:
Phishing remains the most common way attackers get into companies like ours. Most attempts arrive by email, but we also see phishing by text message, by phone, and through fake carrier portal login pages that target our logistics staff.

If you receive a suspicious email, use the Report Phish button in the mail toolbar. This sends the message to the Security team and removes it from your inbox. Do not forward suspicious emails to colleagues, and do not click links or open attachments to check whether they are real. Suspicious text messages or calls can be reported to security@harborpine.example with a screenshot.

Typical signs of phishing include urgent requests to pay an invoice or change supplier bank details, unexpected password reset messages, sender addresses that look almost like ours, and requests to approve an MFA prompt.

The Security team sends simulated phishing emails every month. Clicking a simulated phishing link is not a disciplinary matter, but it does assign a ten-minute refresher course. Employees who fail three simulations within twelve months attend a live thirty-minute session with the Security team. Reporting a simulation through the Report Phish button counts as a pass and shows on the team leaderboard.

If you already clicked a link or entered your password, report it straight away. Change your password, and Security will check your account for unusual sign-ins. Acting within minutes greatly reduces the damage.

documents.title: Personal Devices and Mobile Access (BYOD)
documents.text:
# Personal Devices and Mobile Access (BYOD)

You may use a personal phone or tablet for work email, chat, and calendar, provided it meets these rules. Personal laptops may never be used for work.

## Enrolment

- Install the **Anchor MDM** work profile from the app store and sign in with SSO.
- The work profile separates company apps and data from your personal apps. Security can see the device model, OS version, and whether the device is encrypted. Security **cannot** see personal photos, messages, browsing, or location.

## Minimum requirements

- Operating system no more than **two major versions** behind the current release.
- Screen lock with a PIN of at least 6 digits or biometrics.
- Device not jailbroken or rooted.

## What is allowed on a personal device

| Data class | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Public and Internal | Yes |
| Confidential | Yes, inside work profile apps only |
| Restricted | **No** |

## Leaving the company or losing the device

When you leave, or if you report the device lost, Security removes the work profile. This selective wipe removes only company data; your personal data is untouched.

## Stipend

Employees who are required to be reachable on mobile, such as on-call engineers and warehouse supervisors, receive a **$50 monthly phone stipend**.

## Company-issued phones

Employees whose role needs a phone for warehouse scanning or field work receive a company phone instead of the stipend. Company phones are fully managed, and personal apps are limited to those in the approved catalogue.

documents.title: Access Reviews and Offboarding
documents.text:
Access to Harbor & Pine systems follows the principle of least privilege: people get the access they need for their current role, and nothing more. Two processes keep access accurate over time, quarterly access reviews and offboarding.

Every quarter, system owners receive a list of everyone with access to their system in the access review tool. They must confirm or remove each person within fifteen working days. Systems holding Restricted data, including payroll, the production cloud console, ledger-db, and customer support tools, are reviewed by both the system owner and the person's manager. Access not confirmed by the deadline is removed automatically.

When someone changes roles, their manager requests the new access they need and the access review in the following quarter removes what is no longer needed. Access that is clearly tied to the old role, such as finance approval rights, is removed on the day of the move.

When an employee leaves, People Operations records the termination in Compass. This triggers automatic deprovisioning: single sign-on is disabled and all access is revoked within four hours of the termination time. For involuntary terminations, access is revoked at the start of the termination meeting. Badges are deactivated at the same time.

Departing employees return their laptop, security keys, and badge on their last day. Remote employees receive a prepaid return box. Managers must reassign any shared documents, on-call shifts, and approval workflows owned by the departing employee before their last day.

documents.title: Tidewater Pricing Tiers
documents.text:
# Tidewater Pricing Tiers

Tidewater is Harbor & Pine's shipping management SaaS. It is sold in three tiers. Prices below are list prices in US dollars, billed monthly; annual billing gives a **15% discount**.

| Tier | Price | Included shipments per month | Overage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $49 per month | 500 | $0.12 per shipment |
| Growth | $299 per month | 5,000 | $0.08 per shipment |
| Enterprise | Custom contract | Negotiated, typically 50,000+ | Negotiated |

## What every tier includes

- Multi-carrier rate shopping and label printing
- Tracking page with your branding
- Email support

## Add-ons

- **Route Optimizer:** $0.04 per optimized stop, available on Growth and Enterprise.
- **Customs Pack:** automatic commercial invoices and HS code suggestions, $99 per month.
- **Additional warehouse location:** $50 per month per location on Starter and Growth.

## Changing tiers

Upgrades take effect immediately and are pro-rated. Downgrades take effect at the next billing date. Customers on annual billing can upgrade at any time but can only downgrade at renewal.

## Discounts

Registered non-profits receive 30% off Starter and Growth. Sales can offer up to 10% additional discount on Growth annual plans without approval; anything more needs the Head of Sales.

Plan limits for users, webhooks, and data retention are listed in the feature limits page.

documents.title: Tidewater Service Level Agreement (SLA)
documents.text:
# Tidewater Service Level Agreement (SLA)

The SLA defines the uptime we commit to for Tidewater and the credits customers receive when we miss it. Starter customers have no contractual SLA.

## Uptime commitments

| Tier | Monthly uptime commitment |
|---|---|
| Growth | 99.9% |
| Enterprise | 99.95% |

Uptime is measured per calendar month on the core API and web application. Scheduled maintenance announced at least 5 days in advance, limited to 4 hours per month, is excluded.

## Service credits

| Monthly uptime achieved | Credit (% of monthly fee) |
|---|---|
| Below commitment but at least 99.0% | 10% |
| Below 99.0% but at least 95.0% | 25% |
| Below 95.0% | 50% |

Credits are applied to the next invoice and cannot be exchanged for cash. Total credits in a month cannot exceed 50% of the monthly fee.

## How to claim

The customer must request the credit within **30 days** after the end of the affected month, by emailing support with the dates and times of the outage. Support validates the claim against our monitoring data.

## Exclusions

Outages caused by carrier APIs, customer networks, misuse, or force majeure are not counted. Rate limiting (ERR-3308) is not downtime.

## Support response times

Response-time commitments for support tickets are defined in the support escalation guide, not in this SLA.

documents.title: Tidewater Plan Feature Limits

# Tidewater Plan Feature Limits

This page lists the product limits for each Tidewater tier. For prices see the pricing tiers page; for API request limits see the ERR-3308 article.

| Limit | Starter | Growth | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| User seats | 3 | 25 | Unlimited |
| Warehouse locations included | 1 | 3 | Unlimited |
| Webhook endpoints | 5 | 50 | Unlimited |
| Shipment data retention | 90 days | 1 year | 7 years |
| Custom label templates | 2 | 20 | Unlimited |
| Single sign-on (SAML) | No | No | Yes |
| Audit log | No | 30 days | 1 year |
| Sandbox accounts | 0 | 1 | 3 |

## What happens at a limit

- **Seats:** inviting a user beyond the limit shows an upgrade prompt; existing users are never removed.
- **Webhooks:** creating an extra endpoint fails with a clear error in the dashboard and API.
- **Retention:** shipment records older than the retention period are deleted nightly. Customers are emailed 14 days before their first deletion, and can export data before then.

## Extra seats

Growth customers can buy extra seats at $15 per user per month, up to 50 seats in total. Beyond that, Enterprise is required.

## Changes to limits

Limits may change with notice of at least 60 days; increases may happen at any time.

## Archived data

When an Enterprise customer's contract specifies a longer retention period, data older than 7 years can be moved to cold archive on request. Archived shipments can be restored for reporting within 48 hours, for a fee set in the contract.

documents.title: Tidewater API Keys for Customers
documents.text:
Tidewater API Keys for Customers

Customers authenticate to tidewater-api with API keys created in the Tidewater dashboard under *Settings > Developers*.

Key types

Live keys start with hp_live_ and act on real shipments, creating billable labels.
Test keys start with hp_test_ and work only against the sandbox; labels are void.

Scopes

Each key has one or more scopes: shipments:read, shipments:write, labels:write, tracking:read, and billing:read. Customers should create keys with the smallest set of scopes they need, for example a tracking widget only needs tracking:read.

Rotation

Customers can have up to two active live keys at the same time, so they can rotate without downtime: create a new key, deploy it, then revoke the old one.
We recommend rotating keys every 12 months.
Keys that have not been used for 180 days are disabled automatically, with an email warning 14 days before.

Leaked keys

If a customer reports a leaked key, support should tell them to revoke it immediately in the dashboard. Our scanner also detects hp_live_ keys published in public code repositories and revokes them automatically, emailing the account owner.

Support notes

Support staff can never view a full key; the dashboard shows only the last four characters.

Webhook secrets

Webhook signing secrets are separate from API keys. They are created per endpoint and shown only once, when the endpoint is created or the secret is regenerated. Regenerating a webhook secret does not affect API keys, and revoking an API key does not change webhook secrets.

documents.title: Route Optimizer Add-on
documents.text:
Route Optimizer is an add-on for Tidewater Growth and Enterprise customers who run their own delivery vehicles. It plans multi-stop delivery routes that minimise driving time while respecting delivery windows, vehicle capacity, and driver shift lengths.

Customers upload the day's stops by file or through the API, choose the available vehicles, and Route Optimizer returns an ordered route for each vehicle, usually within two minutes for up to 2,000 stops. Routes can be sent to drivers through the Tidewater Driver mobile app, which shows turn-by-turn navigation and captures proof of delivery with photo and signature.

Pricing is usage based at $0.04 per optimized stop, billed monthly in arrears. Re-optimizing the same stop on the same day is not charged again. There is no minimum commitment and no setup fee, and the add-on can be switched on or off at any time from the billing settings page.

Limits: a single optimization request can contain at most 2,000 stops and 100 vehicles. Each vehicle can have at most one break window. Time windows must be at least fifteen minutes long. Customers with larger fleets should contact their account manager about batch planning.

Route Optimizer uses road network data that is refreshed monthly and traffic patterns averaged by hour and weekday; it does not use live traffic. The add-on is not available for Starter customers, who will see an upgrade prompt if they try to enable it.

Customers can export planned routes as CSV or send them to third-party telematics systems through the routes API. Each route includes the planned arrival time at every stop, the total distance, and the expected return time to the depot. Drivers can reorder stops on the road in the mobile app, and the change is recorded so that dispatchers can see where plans and reality differ. Proof-of-delivery photos are kept for 90 days on Growth and for 1 year on Enterprise.
